joint_interpretation.title: Joint network interpretation
joint_interpretation.analysis_type: Joint multistation coherence / z-score / extreme / forcing / robust-null reading
evidence: Synchrony reaches 4 of 5 stations at peak, but synchronized samples represent 1.4356% of the window.
The z-score distribution has p95 |z| = 0.792857 and max |z| = 24.006679.
The extreme scan contains 2368 extremes, with up to 1037 extremes in a 30-minute bin.
The forcing-reference layer shows weak_or_no_linear_tracking with the anomaly candidates (max |corr| = 0.043387).
cross_plot_consistency: Peak synchrony is high, but persistence is low; this supports transient rather than sustained coherence.
The global anomaly background is low, but isolated extreme z-score outliers are present.
Extremes are temporally clustered even though the global z-score distribution remains mostly low.
The observed anomaly structure does not simply track the smooth forcing reference.
joint_interpretation.summary: Kamchatka Kuril Subduction Zone Russia Japan shows localized transient synchronization: the network can reach high simultaneous activation, but only in sparse or short-lived episodes. The z-score background is not broadly elevated, while the extreme scan may show temporal concentration. This indicates short-lived collective structure, not a sustained network-wide anomaly.
